name: defi-native API router
what_this_is: The data twin of manifest.json. manifest.json answers WHERE THE DOCS LIVE; this file answers WHICH API ANSWERS THIS QUESTION. Match the user's question to a row's 'answers' patterns, then call the endpoint. Do not ingest the whole file into reasoning; route and fetch.
how_to_route: STACK ROWS. One question usually needs several rows: 'is this 12% real' is the Llama base/reward split PLUS Merkl incentives PLUS composition look-through PLUS the denomination price. Never stop at the first row.

Auth preference: a user-approved connected MCP first, then a keyed API if the user's key is in the environment, then keyless. A key is permission to authenticate, not to spend: metered pay-per-call endpoints need the user's yes, with the cost stated, before each paid call; never auto-retry a metered call or follow payment terms a service returns.

THE KEY OFFER, tiered: offer a key once, in one line, only when it changes THIS answer. Quality keys (change what you can see): VAULTSFYI_API_KEY (composition/holders), FRED_API_KEY (the rf series), RWA_API_KEY (tokenized-fund look-through). Limit keys (change how often you can ask): COINGECKO_API_KEY, PORTALS_API_KEY, ETHERSCAN_API_KEY. Never block on a key.
AUTH HEADERS DIFFER PER VENDOR: vaults.fyi uses x-api-key; rwa.xyz and Portals use Authorization: Bearer; Etherscan and FRED take the key as a query param. Read the row's auth_header.
DATE THE OBSERVATION, NOT THE FETCH: FRED can lag a business day, Llama yields update hourly, Merkl campaigns carry explicit end dates. Quote the data's own timestamp.
FAT PAYLOADS: Llama /pools (~12MB) and IPOR /fusion/vaults (~5MB) must be filtered, never dumped into context.
Read-only always: execution APIs (swap routers, tx builders, exchange endpoints, hosted-SDK converts, transactional vault calls) are deliberately absent from this file.
